correctness.rationale: Averaging a projection over sign translations forces the cubic Fourier projector. Its Krawtchouk kernel is (S_n^3-(3n-2)S_n)/6. Uniform local binomial Stirling/Edgeworth expansion through n^-1, Hoeffding tail truncation, and derivative jumps phi(0), 2phi(sqrt(3)) at three absolute-value cusps produce the stated n^-1 correction. Gaussian integral evaluation and shifted Euler–Maclaurin B_2 phases give the precise coefficient. Every fixed-parity phase is approximated by nearest integers of that parity to (2k+2theta+eps)^2/3, obtaining the stated interval endpoints and strict gap. Independent numerical comparisons of exact binomial expectation against phase asymptotics at n=100,101,400,401,1000,1001 showed decaying normalized discrepancies, not proof of the asymptotic.
residual_risks: Uniformity of the local Stirling expansion and cusp-summation O(h^3) remainder must hold on the stated truncated lattice; proof provides cutoffs but no explicit uniform constants.
Only real homogeneous degree three, uniform cube, n->infinity; finite diagnostics do not establish the limit.

value.rationale: The degree-three Walsh projection constant is a natural Banach-space invariant whose leading asymptotic is known; computing an oscillatory sharp second-order term and two disjoint parity bands rules out a single finite-size correction. Three cusp contributions and moving irrational-scale phase are mathematically nontrivial beyond the known first order.
residual_risks: No third-order uniform error constant or extension to higher Walsh degree is claimed.

final_claim: For real degree-three Walsh projection constants lambda_n, an explicit order-sqrt(n) Edgeworth plus Bernoulli cusp-lattice correction yields disjoint, completely attained even/odd subsequential limit intervals; the leading c n^(3/2) is not claimed as new.
limitations: Real degree-three only; asymptotic remainder o(sqrt(n)) and no explicit uniform finite-size constant.
